description:
FOUND s496a (Opus, 2026-09-26), member 3 of #2060.

`\X` is now perl's LEGACY approximation `(?>\r\n|\P{M}\p{M}*|\p{M}+)` (a base character with its combining marks), which the Unicode property support (#2060) made possible.  It is still NOT UAX #29 extended grapheme clusters, and these differ from perl 5.40.3:

    sub m1 { ($_[0] =~ $_[1]) ? 1 : 0 }
    print m1("\x{1F1E6}\x{1F1E8}", qr/^\X$/), " ",                  # regional-indicator PAIR
          scalar(() = "\x{1100}\x{1161}" =~ /\X/g), " ",            # Hangul L + V
          scalar(() = "\x{1F468}\x{200D}\x{1F469}" =~ /\X/g), "\n"; # emoji ZWJ sequence
  perl:        1 1 1
  PCL s496a:   0 2 3

A faithful \X needs the Grapheme_Cluster_Break property (gcb=, NOT generated by tools/rebuild-uniprops today -- it is in the "dies" list) plus the UAX #29 rules GB3-GB13 (Extend, SpacingMark, Prepend, L/V/T/LV/LVT, ZWJ + Extended_Pictographic, RI pairs).  cl-ppcre has no grapheme primitive, so it is either a pattern built from gcb classes (the RI-pair and ZWJ rules are expressible; GB9c/Indic conjuncts are 15.1, not 15.0) or a filter function.  Generate gcb= and ExtPict first (tools/rebuild-uniprops, a one-line change to @ENUM_PROPS), then build the pattern.
docs/not-supported.md's `\X` row names this task.
subject: \X is the legacy approximation (base + combining marks) since s496a, not UAX #29: a regional-indicator pair, a Hangul L+V syllable and an emoji ZWJ sequence are one cluster in perl and several in PCL
